note: Review-only companion; not a TestsData row. Correct-answer rationales included; full distractor-specific manual audit remains required before production insertion.

questions.text: Which component executes instructions and coordinates processing?
questions.rationale: The CPU executes program instructions.

questions.text: Which memory normally loses its contents when power is removed?
questions.rationale: RAM is volatile working memory.

questions.text: Which software manages hardware resources and services for applications?
questions.rationale: The operating system manages hardware and application execution.

questions.text: Which device is primarily used to enter text?
questions.rationale: A keyboard is an input device.

questions.text: Which storage device has no moving mechanical platters?
questions.rationale: An SSD stores data electronically, without spinning platters.

questions.text: Which Linux command displays the current working directory?
questions.rationale: pwd prints the present working directory.

questions.text: In vi, which key enters Insert mode before the cursor?
questions.rationale: Press i to insert text at the cursor.

questions.text: Which command creates a directory in a Linux shell?
questions.rationale: mkdir creates a directory.

questions.text: What normally happens when a file is deleted to the Windows Recycle Bin?

options.label: B
options.text: It can usually be restored from the bin

questions.rationale: The Recycle Bin retains eligible deleted items until restored or permanently removed.

questions.text: Which device displays visual output from a computer?
questions.rationale: A monitor is an output display.

questions.text: Which Word alignment makes text even at both left and right margins?
questions.rationale: Justify aligns text to both margins.

questions.text: Which feature copies formatting from one selection to another in Word?
questions.rationale: Format Painter copies formatting attributes.

questions.text: Where does a document header normally appear?

options.label: A
options.text: At the bottom of the page

questions.rationale: A header appears in the top margin area.

questions.text: Where does a footer normally appear?
questions.rationale: A footer occupies the bottom margin area.

questions.text: Which feature can place faint text such as CONFIDENTIAL behind document text?
questions.rationale: A watermark can place faint text or an image behind content.

questions.text: Which setting controls vertical space between lines of a paragraph?
questions.rationale: Line spacing sets the distance between lines.

questions.text: Which layout is suitable for newspaper-style text in two vertical blocks?
questions.rationale: Columns create side-by-side vertical text blocks.

questions.text: How can Word use a different header on the first page?
questions.rationale: Different First Page separates first-page header/footer content.

questions.text: Which view helps inspect page layout before printing?
questions.rationale: Print Preview shows how pages are expected to print.

questions.text: Which control changes the font size of selected text?
questions.rationale: The Font Size control changes the selected text size.

questions.text: Which Excel formula adds values in cells B2 through B6?
questions.rationale: SUM adds values in the range.

questions.text: Which formula calculates the mean of C2 through C7?
questions.rationale: AVERAGE returns the arithmetic mean.

questions.text: Which reference stays fixed when a formula is copied in any direction?
questions.rationale: An absolute reference fixes both column and row.

questions.text: Which Excel function returns the current date without a time component?
questions.rationale: TODAY returns the current date.

questions.text: Which function returns the current date and time?
questions.rationale: NOW returns current date and time.

questions.text: Which feature keeps row headings visible while scrolling down?
questions.rationale: Freeze Panes keeps selected rows or columns visible.

questions.text: Which operation places employee names in alphabetical order?
questions.rationale: Sort A to Z orders text alphabetically.

questions.text: Which feature displays only worksheet rows that meet a condition?
questions.rationale: A filter hides rows that do not meet the criteria.

questions.text: A chart compares enrolment across separate departments. Which is usually clearest?
questions.rationale: Bar and column charts compare values across categories.

questions.text: Which Excel function sums values only when an associated category meets a criterion?
questions.rationale: SUMIF adds values that meet a specified condition.

questions.text: In PowerPoint, which feature controls recurring design elements across slides?
questions.rationale: Slide Master controls shared layouts and recurring design.

questions.text: Which PowerPoint feature makes a clicked image open a website?
questions.rationale: A hyperlink connects an object to a web or file destination.

questions.text: Which feature applies movement or emphasis to an object on a slide?
questions.rationale: Animations control effects on slide objects.

questions.text: Which email field hides recipients from other recipients?
questions.rationale: BCC recipients are not shown to other recipients.

questions.text: Which email field sends a visible copy to additional recipients?
questions.rationale: CC adds visible copy recipients.

questions.text: What is an email attachment?

options.label: B
options.text: A file sent with the message

questions.rationale: An attachment is a file included with an email.

questions.text: What does an email signature usually do?

options.label: C
options.text: Adds saved sender details to messages

questions.rationale: A signature appends saved contact or sign-off text.

questions.text: Which HTML element represents a paragraph?
questions.rationale: The p element represents a paragraph.

questions.text: Which CSS property sets an element's background colour?
questions.rationale: background-color controls background colour.

questions.text: What is a browser search query primarily used for?

options.label: A
options.text: To locate relevant pages using keywords

questions.rationale: Search queries help locate relevant webpages.

questions.text: A student accidentally deletes a project folder using normal Windows deletion. Where should they check first?
questions.rationale: Normally deleted items are often recoverable from the Recycle Bin.

questions.text: In File Explorer, how can a user select several non-adjacent files?

options.label: A
options.text: Hold Ctrl while clicking each file

options.label: B
options.text: Hold Shift and click the first and last

questions.rationale: Ctrl-click selects separate items individually.

questions.text: A desktop shortcut is deleted but the original document remains. Why?

options.label: C
options.text: Deleting the shortcut usually removes only the link

questions.rationale: A shortcut points to the original item rather than containing its full data.

questions.text: A Linux command must list files, then enter a directory named reports. Which sequence fits?
questions.rationale: ls lists contents and cd changes the working directory.

questions.text: A user needs detailed file listings including hidden entries in a Unix shell. Which command is best?
questions.rationale: ls -la lists hidden entries and detailed metadata.

questions.text: Windows is to be installed on a laptop containing irreplaceable files. What should be done before changing partitions?

options.label: B
options.text: Back up important files and verify the target partition

questions.rationale: Installation or partition changes may destroy data; back up and confirm the target.

questions.text: A user wants to adjust display output to 1280×960. Where should they look first?
questions.rationale: Display resolution is configured in display settings.

questions.text: Which action most directly reduces risk from a known OS security vulnerability?
questions.rationale: Trusted security updates patch known vulnerabilities.

questions.text: A file's exact location and size must be checked without opening it. Which feature is appropriate?
questions.rationale: File Properties reports metadata such as size.

questions.text: A Unix directory name contains a space. Which command style treats it as one path?

options.label: C
options.text: Use a file-manager search as a shell command

questions.rationale: Quoting the path prevents the shell splitting it at the space.

questions.text: A three-page newsletter needs two columns on each page and a title across the top. Which layout approach best fits the body?

options.label: A
options.text: Apply columns to the body and keep the title in a separate heading area

options.label: B
options.text: Put every paragraph inside a screenshot

options.label: C
options.text: Use a different font for each line

questions.rationale: Separate title and body formatting so columns affect the newsletter text.

questions.text: A report's first page must have no footer, while later pages show page numbers. What is the most direct Word setting?

options.label: B
options.text: Use Different First Page, then add numbering to later-page footers

options.label: D
options.text: Put page numbers in every paragraph

questions.rationale: Different First Page allows the first-page footer to differ.

questions.text: A document needs one header on odd pages and another on even pages. Which feature supports this?
questions.rationale: Different Odd & Even Pages enables alternating header/footer content.

questions.text: A document is printed first as page 1 only, then as a complete landscape document. Which sequence fits?

options.label: A
options.text: Print all pages portrait, then page 1 only

options.label: B
options.text: Change font to landscape, then export a screenshot

options.label: C
options.text: Print page 1 for the first job, then set landscape and print all pages

questions.rationale: Print range controls the first job; orientation controls the second.

questions.text: A paragraph's formatting must be reused without copying its text. What is the best tool?
questions.rationale: Format Painter copies formatting rather than the text.

questions.text: A report title looks right on page 1 but later headings differ. What most helps keep all headings consistent?

options.label: B
options.text: Insert a screenshot of every heading

options.label: C
options.text: Use a consistent built-in or custom heading style

options.label: D
options.text: Put each title in the footer

questions.rationale: Styles apply consistent formatting to matching headings.

questions.text: A Word sales table must be ranked by annual sales. What should be sorted?

options.label: A
options.text: The full table by its sales column

questions.rationale: Sorting complete rows preserves each product's corresponding data.

questions.text: A newsletter needs the word CONFIDENTIAL faintly behind text on every page. Which feature is suitable?
questions.rationale: A watermark is intended for background text or graphics.

questions.text: A one-page document prints with text too close to the edge. What should be checked first?

options.label: C
options.text: Page margins and printer printable area

questions.rationale: Margins and the printer's printable area affect the edge spacing.

questions.text: A three-page document needs its title and author details repeated at the top of later pages. Where should they go?

options.label: C
options.text: A text box at the end

questions.rationale: Headers are designed for recurring page-level content.

questions.text: A copied formula multiplies each row's amount by the fixed tax rate in B1. Which reference keeps B1 fixed?
questions.rationale: $B$1 fixes both the column and row.

questions.text: Marks in B2:G2 are out of 100 each. Which formula calculates their percentage correctly?
questions.rationale: Divide total marks by the 600 possible marks and multiply by 100.

questions.text: Column A lists departments and column B lists expenses. Sum expenses for IT only. Which formula fits?
questions.rationale: SUMIF matches IT in A and adds matching values in B.

questions.text: A row has six subject marks in B2:G2. Which formula calculates the total?
questions.rationale: SUM adds the six marks.

questions.text: H2 contains a percentage. Which formula returns Pass at 35% or above, otherwise Fail?
questions.rationale: The threshold condition is H2>=35%.

questions.text: A student's percentage is 68%. Required bands are Distinction ≥70%, First Class ≥60%, Second Class ≥50%, Pass ≥35%, else Fail. Which result applies?
questions.rationale: 68% is at least 60% and below 70%.

questions.text: A worksheet must keep columns A and B visible while scrolling horizontally. What should the user do?

options.label: A
options.text: Freeze Panes from a selection immediately right of column B

questions.rationale: Freezing panes from column C locks columns A and B.

questions.text: A staff list should display employees hired after 1 January 2025 without deleting other records. What should be used?

options.label: B
options.text: Filter by the Hire Date condition

questions.rationale: Filtering hides nonmatching rows without deleting them.

questions.text: A chart compares marks for six subjects in one class. Which is generally most direct?
questions.rationale: Column charts compare values across discrete categories.

questions.text: A cell must show the current date and time and update when recalculated. Which function is appropriate?
questions.rationale: NOW returns both current date and time.

questions.text: A basic HTML page needs a background colour and an image. Which approach is appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Set CSS background-color and background-image on the page body

options.label: B
options.text: Put both values in the page title

options.label: C
options.text: Use a p element as a file-system command

questions.rationale: CSS can set both background colour and image.

questions.text: A presentation's logo and footer should appear consistently across slides. Where should they go?

options.label: A
options.text: Separately pasted only on the first slide

options.label: B
options.text: Slide Master or a shared layout

questions.rationale: Slide Master and layouts manage shared elements.

questions.text: A clicked image in PowerPoint should open a specified webpage. What should be added?
questions.rationale: A hyperlink associates the image with a destination.

questions.text: An invitation email goes to five friends, but the coordinator must receive a hidden copy. Which field should contain the coordinator?
questions.rationale: BCC hides that recipient from other recipients.

questions.text: An email asks recipients to open a venue map document. What must the sender do if the file should travel with the message?

options.label: A
options.text: Attach the map document and verify it is attached

options.label: B
options.text: Put the file path only in the subject

options.label: C
options.text: Add the map to the signature but send no file

options.label: D
options.text: Use CC as a file upload

questions.rationale: The document must be attached to the email.

questions.text: A user wants search results from official Digital India portal pages rather than unrelated social posts. Which strategy is stronger?

options.label: B
options.text: Use specific service keywords and check relevant official domains

options.label: C
options.text: Click the first result without checking its domain

questions.rationale: Specific search terms and domain checks improve relevance.

questions.text: An email signature should append the sender's name, class and contact details. What should be configured?
questions.rationale: A saved signature can be appended to outgoing messages.

questions.text: A group should enter details in a shared spreadsheet. What should the owner verify before sharing?

options.label: B
options.text: Public access is enabled for all

options.label: C
options.text: The workbook has no header row

options.label: D
options.text: Intended members have suitable edit permission and link scope is limited

questions.rationale: Appropriate permissions permit the desired changes without broad exposure.

questions.text: Which HTML element inserts an image when a valid source is supplied?
questions.rationale: The img element embeds an image.

questions.text: What should a user enter to open a known website directly from the browser address bar?
questions.rationale: The URL or domain directs the browser to that site.

questions.text: A Windows PC is slow after startup. The user wants evidence about resource use before uninstalling software. What is the best first check?

options.label: B
options.text: Open Task Manager and compare process CPU/memory usage

questions.rationale: Task Manager can identify resource-heavy processes before changes are made.

questions.text: An installer asks to format a partition that may contain personal files. What is the safest response?

options.label: A
options.text: Continue because setup always protects files

options.label: C
options.text: Stop, verify the target disk and back up files before formatting

questions.rationale: Formatting can destroy data; confirm the target and backups first.

questions.text: A user empties the Recycle Bin and the original file is no longer visible. Which statement is most accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: It is guaranteed to be easily restored from the bin

options.label: B
options.text: Emptying the bin removes the normal restore path; recovery may require backups or recovery tools

options.label: C
options.text: It must be attached to an email

questions.rationale: Emptying the bin removes the simple restore path; recovery is not guaranteed.

questions.text: A shell command fails because a directory name contains spaces. Which correction treats it as one argument?
questions.rationale: Quoting the path prevents shell argument splitting at the space.

questions.text: A vi user has unwanted edits and wants to quit without saving. Which command is appropriate from command mode?
questions.rationale: :q! exits without saving unsaved changes.

questions.text: A workstation is shared by several students. Which setup reduces risk of one user's files being changed by another?

options.label: B
options.text: Give all users full administrator rights

options.label: D
options.text: Use separate accounts with least privilege and screen locking

questions.rationale: Separate accounts and least privilege limit unintended access.

questions.text: A pop-up tells the user to install a security patch from an unknown site. What is safest?

options.label: A
options.text: Download it because the pop-up says urgent

options.label: B
options.text: Close it and use trusted OS/vendor update channels

questions.rationale: Use trusted update sources, not unsolicited pop-ups.

questions.text: A Linux user wants to inspect permissions and file details, including hidden entries, before changing access. Which command is safest?
questions.rationale: ls -la inspects details without modifying files.

questions.text: A computer has no usable display after a resolution change. Which recovery attempt is most appropriate first?

options.label: C
options.text: Use display recovery/safe mode or revert to a supported resolution

questions.rationale: Reverting to a supported display mode addresses the configuration problem.

questions.text: Collaborators may edit one spreadsheet but must not manage users or delete the source folder. Which permission design is best?

options.label: D
options.text: Grant edit access to the intended spreadsheet only and limit sharing scope

questions.rationale: Least-privilege sharing limits permissions to what is needed.

questions.text: A three-page newsletter needs a title, a two-column body, a first-page-only header and page numbers on later pages. Which plan is most robust?

options.label: A
options.text: Use a heading for the title, columns for the body, Different First Page, then number later-page footers

options.label: B
options.text: Insert each page as an image

options.label: C
options.text: Use three different files without page settings

options.label: D
options.text: Put every requirement in the title

questions.rationale: These features address title/body layout and distinct first-page header/footer behavior.

questions.text: A report needs odd-page header 'Your investment', even-page header 'Small Savings', and page numbers in the footer. Which combination fits?

options.label: B
options.text: Different Odd & Even Pages plus footer page numbering

questions.rationale: Odd/even headers and footer numbering meet the requirements.

questions.text: A document must print page 1 for a proof, then the whole document in landscape. What must be verified between jobs?

options.label: B
options.text: That all pages but page 1 are deleted

options.label: C
options.text: Print range 1 first, then All pages with landscape orientation

questions.rationale: Print range and orientation are separate settings.

questions.text: A report title has the right style on page 1 but later headings differ. What best keeps headings consistent?

options.label: A
options.text: Format each heading with random settings

options.label: C
options.text: Copy the whole first page repeatedly

options.label: D
options.text: Apply a shared heading style and modify that style when needed

questions.rationale: Styles maintain consistent formatting across headings.

questions.text: A three-page document needs a watermark and distinct first-page header. What should be configured?

options.label: A
options.text: Watermark in design/page-background controls and Different First Page for the header

options.label: B
options.text: A different font in each paragraph

options.label: C
options.text: A text box only on page 1

questions.rationale: The watermark and first-page header are separate features.

questions.text: A Word sales table must be ranked by annual total while each product keeps its figures. What is essential?

options.label: B
options.text: Select the whole table and sort by the total field

options.label: C
options.text: Copy totals into a new document

questions.rationale: Sorting the whole table preserves each row's relationship.

questions.text: Pagination changes unexpectedly after a layout edit. What should be inspected before deleting text?

options.label: C
options.text: Check page/section breaks, paragraph spacing and margins

questions.rationale: Breaks and spacing can change pagination.

questions.text: The first page should have no header, but later pages should show title and author. What setting is key?

options.label: A
options.text: Different First Page, with title and author in the regular header

questions.rationale: The regular header then serves subsequent pages.

questions.text: Body text should have two columns, but the title should span the full page. What avoids placing the title in a narrow column?

options.label: A
options.text: Put the title in every paragraph

options.label: B
options.text: Keep the title in its heading/section and apply columns to the body area

options.label: C
options.text: Convert the title to a footer

questions.rationale: Separate title and body layout so the title spans the page.

questions.text: A document looks correct on screen but is clipped when printed. Which checks are most relevant?

options.label: D
options.text: Print Preview, margins, paper size and printer printable area

questions.rationale: Layout and printer settings determine print output.

questions.text: Marks in B2:G2 are out of 100 each. Which formula calculates the percentage correctly?
questions.rationale: Total marks are divided by the 600 possible marks then multiplied by 100.

questions.text: Which nested IF implements Distinction ≥70%, First ≥60%, Second ≥50%, Pass ≥35%, otherwise Fail?
questions.rationale: Descending thresholds preserve the required bands.

questions.text: A copied formula multiplies each student's amount by a fixed tax rate in B1. Which formula is safe to fill down from D2?
questions.rationale: $B$1 fixes the tax-rate cell as the formula moves.

questions.text: Sum values in F:F only for rows where A equals CE. Which formula is correct?
questions.rationale: SUMIF matches CE in A and sums corresponding values in F.

questions.text: A percentage formula returns 0.68, displayed as 68%. What is the correct interpretation?

options.label: B
options.text: 0.68 equals 68%; percentage formatting displays it as 68%

questions.rationale: Excel stores 68% as 0.68.

questions.text: A result formula labels 68% as Distinction although that threshold is 70%. What should be checked first?

options.label: B
options.text: Condition order and threshold values in the nested IF

options.label: D
options.text: Whether the sheet has a chart

questions.rationale: A wrongly ordered or typed threshold may misclassify the value.

questions.text: Columns A and B must remain visible when scrolling horizontally. Where should the user select before Freeze Panes?

options.label: B
options.text: In C1 or an appropriate cell to the right of column B

options.label: C
options.text: In the last used cell only

questions.rationale: Freeze Panes locks columns to the left of the selected cell.

questions.text: A line chart is requested for six subject categories that are not time points. Which chart is usually easier to interpret?

options.label: A
options.text: A bar/column chart with labelled subjects

options.label: B
options.text: A line chart implying continuous time

questions.rationale: Bars compare discrete categories without implying a time sequence.

questions.text: A table needs sorting by Hire Date and filtering by Designation. Which approach is appropriate?

options.label: B
options.text: Use table sort/filter controls on the full records

questions.rationale: Sorting and filtering complete records preserve employee fields.

questions.text: A formula is copied down, but each row still uses the same candidate's marks. What should be examined first?

options.label: A
options.text: Whether a row reference was accidentally made absolute

options.label: B
options.text: Whether the sheet has a watermark

questions.rationale: An unintended absolute row reference can keep the formula tied to one candidate.

questions.text: A group must co-edit a spreadsheet, but other students must not edit it. What is the safest sharing plan?

options.label: A
options.text: Publish an editable link to anyone

options.label: B
options.text: Share with intended group members, grant only needed edit access, and verify link scope

options.label: D
options.text: Make every member an account owner

questions.rationale: Specific recipients and least privilege limit unintended changes.

questions.text: A ten-slide deck needs a consistent logo/footer and four images need motion effects. What is best?

options.label: A
options.text: Manually recreate every footer and animate all text

options.label: B
options.text: Use Slide Master/shared layouts and animate only the four specified images

options.label: D
options.text: Use slide transitions instead of object animations

questions.rationale: Master layouts manage repeated design; object animations control selected images.

questions.text: An email must go to five friends, show faculty a copy, hide the coordinator, and include a route document. Which setup meets all conditions?

options.label: A
options.text: Friends in To, faculty in CC, coordinator in BCC, route file attached

options.label: C
options.text: Coordinator in CC, faculty in BCC, route only in subject

options.label: D
options.text: Route document in signature, all recipients in BCC

questions.rationale: To, CC, BCC and attachment fields each meet one requirement.

questions.text: A page should have a background image while keeping a paragraph readable. Which implementation is best?

options.label: A
options.text: Place image markup after closing the HTML document

options.label: B
options.text: Set the background image in CSS and keep text contrast readable

options.label: C
options.text: Use the image as the only text content

options.label: D
options.text: Set the document title to the image URL

questions.rationale: CSS background imagery preserves text content; contrast must remain sufficient.

questions.text: An official-looking e-governance site asks for credentials. What should a user verify before signing in?

options.label: C
options.text: That its domain/URL is authentic and the service is expected

questions.rationale: Authentic domain checks help distinguish legitimate services from lookalikes.

questions.text: A browser search returns irrelevant pages for an assignment. What is likely to narrow results?

options.label: A
options.text: Add specific subject terms and quote an exact phrase when helpful; verify domains

questions.rationale: Specific terms and phrase searches reduce irrelevant results.

questions.text: A PowerPoint image should jump to a later slide with detailed data. Which approach is best?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a hyperlink to the target slide

options.label: C
options.text: Change only the slide master font

questions.rationale: A hyperlink can point to a location within the presentation.

questions.text: An urgent email claims its attachment is an OS patch. What should the recipient do before opening it?

options.label: A
options.text: Open because urgent email is trusted

options.label: D
options.text: Verify sender and file through a trusted channel first

questions.rationale: Unexpected software attachments should be independently verified.

questions.text: A colleague should view a spreadsheet but must not edit cells. Which permission fits?
questions.rationale: Viewer access allows inspection without editing.

questions.text: A task requires visiting five websites and writing a summary. Which approach gives the most reliable evidence?

options.label: C
options.text: Read relevant pages, record actual domains and compare important claims

questions.rationale: Consulting source pages and verifying domains is stronger than relying on snippets alone.
